tools.name: list_documents
tools.description:
List the user's documents. By default returns ACTIVE docs in their default organization (team org if they have one, personal otherwise). Use `which` to switch lens:
  • 'active'         — default. Docs the user owns or is an org member on. Has the user's own work.
  • 'trash'          — recently-trashed docs. Use when the user says "what did I delete" / "restore X" / "undelete".
  • 'shared-with-me' — docs OTHER people shared with this user (cross-org grants).

Returns slug, name, url, type, language, owner attribution, and latest-version summary for each. Use this to find an existing doc's `slug` before calling `read_document`, `manage_document`, `manage_sharing`, or an authoring tool.

tools.name: get_pdf
tools.description:
DISPLAY a PDF to the user by slug — a SHOW tool, not a read. Renders it inline entirely OFF your context (bytes go to the widget, never into the conversation). Returns the doc's metadata + a REFERENCE to its latest artifact (id, signed fileUrl, metadata) — never the document text.

Use it when the user asks to SEE this doc ("show me / open / pull up X"). `get_pdf` ONLY shows a PDF — a wrong-type call answers with the right show tool to use instead. To load the CONTENTS into your context (to summarize, answer questions, or revise) call `read_document` instead — it reads SILENTLY, rendering nothing. (`app` bundles have no inline preview — share their url.)

tools.name: read_document
tools.description:
Read a document's CONTENT into your context by slug — a SILENT read: NOTHING is rendered or shown to the user (no widget, no preview, no link card). This is the right FIRST call whenever you need the text to reason over — to summarize it, answer questions about it, or edit it into a new version (edit → then call the matching create_* tool with this SAME slug).

Returns the doc's metadata, a reference to its latest artifact (id, signed fileUrl, metadata), `content` — the full body text — for text-like kinds (html/md/text + agent-authored pdf print-HTML + the xlsx/docx specs; binary uploads aren't text-extractable), and any unresolved lint `errors` on the latest version (this is ALSO the way to re-check errors mid-fix-loop — no separate errors tool).

Pass `withHistory: true` to also include the activity feed — every event newest-first (type, timestamp, author, and for content_pushed events the `artifactId` used by manage_document action='revert'). To DISPLAY the doc to the user instead, call the matching `get_*` show tool (get_pdf / get_page / get_sheet / …) — it renders inline entirely off your context.

withHistory.description: If true, also include the activity history (event feed with artifact ids) in the response.

tools.name: screenshot_document
tools.description:
SCREENSHOT a staged document by slug — the rendered result comes back AS IMAGES for your own review, plus the deterministic `errors`. Renders the latest pushed version and returns:
  • `errors` — problems detected at render time. PDF: fixed-page geometry (text past the page edge, text-on-text overlap, content overprinting a bottom-pinned footer, broken images, off-page/clipped elements, blank pages, an underfilled page with a big blank band, sub-legible text, a page scaled down to fit). HTML/APP: viewport + runtime checks (horizontal blowout on desktop or mobile, missing viewport meta, broken images, a blank render, uncaught boot exceptions, missing bundle files, console errors). ALL advisory — nothing blocks a stash; fix them when iterating, never by stripping design.
  • screenshots delivered to YOU as image content — PDF: one per page, up to 8 pages per call. A bare call serves pages 1-8; pass `firstPage`/`lastPage` to pick pages yourself (the user says "pages 5-8 are broken", or you want the next window of a longer doc). When the doc has more pages than one call ships, the result names the range sent (`pageRange`) — keep calling with new ranges until you have seen every page you need. Everything else: a bounded full-height shot at DESKTOP and at MOBILE (390px) — so you can SEE the result and catch what the checks cannot: hidden text, wrong colours, a broken visual layout.

Call it after authoring or iterating a PDF, page, or app to check your work BEFORE telling the user it is ready — especially when a create tool reported errors. The images return to YOU (the model); they are NOT the user-facing inline widget.

slug.description: The doc's 6-char slug (from a create_* result / list_documents / a docstash URL).

firstPage.description: PDF only, optional: 1-based first page of the range to screenshot — use when specific pages need review (the user says "pages 5-8 are broken") or to fetch the next window of a longer doc. Omit for the first 8 pages.

lastPage.description: PDF only, optional: 1-based last page of the explicit range (defaults to firstPage — a single page). At most 8 pages ship per call.

tools.name: list_org_members
tools.description:
List members of the user's default organization — their names AND emails. Use this to figure out WHO TO SHARE WITH when the user says "share with the team" / "who's on this organization?" / "share with Alice" (and you need to resolve Alice → email).

Returns nothing useful for a personal organization (just the user themselves). For team organizations returns the full member roster.

Use the emails returned here as the `email` argument to `manage_sharing` action='add'.

tools.name: manage_document
tools.description:
Doc-level actions other than upload. Pass the `slug` plus an `action`:

  • 'rename'  — change the doc's name. Requires `name`. No new version minted (metadata only). Use when the user says "rename X to Y".
  • 'trash'   — soft-delete. Doc disappears from active list, shows up in `list_documents` with which='trash'. RECOVERABLE — don't tell the user it's permanently gone.
  • 'restore' — un-trash. Mirror of 'trash'. Find the slug via `list_documents` with which='trash'.
  • 'revert'  — repoint the doc at an EARLIER artifact. Requires `artifactId` (get it from `read_document` with withHistory:true — each content_pushed event carries `payload.artifactId`). No bytes move; the server bumps that artifact's refCount and logs a content_pushed event. History stays intact.

For UPLOADING content (create a new doc, push a new version), use the separate `stash` tool — NOT this one.

action.description: Which action to perform on the doc.

name.description: Required when action='rename'. The new name (up to 200 chars).

artifactId.description: Required when action='revert'. The full id of the artifact to revert to (from `read_document` with withHistory:true).

tools.name: manage_sharing
tools.description:
Share AND PUBLISH a doc — this is the ONLY tool that makes a doc public. Use it to PUBLISH / make public / get a public shareable link (action='set-public', isPublic=true), and to grant/revoke per-user access. Pass `slug` + `action`:

  • 'list'        — list all per-user grants (Viewers + Editors). Does NOT include public-link state (use `read_document` for that — it's on `document.isPublic`).
  • 'add'         — grant a specific person access. Requires `email`. Optional `level: 'read' | 'write'` (default 'read'). The recipient must be a DocStash user (sign in once at app.docstash.ai). NOT a public link.
  • 'revoke'      — revoke a per-user grant by `email`. Mirror of 'add'.
  • 'set-public'  — PUBLISH / unpublish the doc: toggle its PUBLIC LINK. Requires `isPublic: boolean`. true = PUBLISH — anyone with the URL sees the latest version (anonymous, no sign-in); false = revoke the public link. This is the ONLY way to make a doc publicly viewable — a bare stashed url stays private. The doc must be saved (stashed) first; you can't publish an unsaved version. Per-doc only — no version-pinned public links.

Call this when the user explicitly asks to PUBLISH, make public, get a public/shareable link, or share/revoke per-user access. Don't infer sharing from vague phrasing like "can you give Alice access" without checking what level they want.

email.description: Required when action='add' or 'revoke'. The grantee's email.

level.description: Optional, only meaningful when action='add'. 'read' (Viewer) or 'write' (Editor). Default 'read'.

isPublic.description: Required when action='set-public'. true = enable public link; false = revoke.

tools.name: create_pdf
tools.description:
Generate a beautiful, print-ready PDF document for DocStash and show the user an INLINE PREVIEW: reports, memos, proposals, letters, résumés, whitepapers, contracts, essays, one-pagers. THIS IS THE DEFAULT for a generic 'make me a document' / 'make me a PDF' request (use `create_docx` only when the user specifically wants an editable WORD doc, `create_text` for markdown/code source, `create_page` for a web page). `content` = a complete self-contained `` document — you author it in HTML/CSS and DocStash renders + presents it AS A PDF (paginated paper, page nav, zoom, one-click PDF download). Do NOT generate a binary .pdf; the user drag-and-drops pre-existing .pdf files on the dashboard. This is a REAL HTML/CSS/JS document rendered by a full Chromium engine and baked to PDF — you have the SAME toolkit a web page has (any CSS layout, SVG, gradients, filters, web fonts, images, JS), NOT a limited document format. The ONLY difference from a live web page is GEOMETRY: it is a fixed A4 sheet that never scrolls or reflows. The structural rules below cover that fixed page. PAGE CONTRACT — a PDF is a FIXED A4 sheet, not a reflowing web page. These are the STRUCTURAL rules for correct rendering: • Wrap EACH page in its own `
…
` (or `
`). DocStash frames every `.ds-page` as a real A4 sheet (portrait, 794×1123px @96dpi) — centered on a canvas, with page nav, fit-to-width scaling on any screen, and a PDF download. Emit N of them for an N-page document. • TYPE SCALE — the sheet is 794px wide and A4 is 210mm, so **1 CSS px = 0.75pt**. Every size you write is three-quarters of what it looks like: `11px` body copy PRINTS AT 8.25pt. Size in px but think in pt: body copy ≈13–15px (≈10–11pt), never below 11px for anything a reader must read; 9px (≈7pt) is the floor for incidental labels/footers. • A PDF page does NOT reflow — it is fixed geometry. Author for a FIXED A4 page: keep each page within ~1123px tall, and when content runs longer SPLIT it into multiple `.ds-page` blocks yourself (you decide where pages break). If one page overflows, DocStash shrinks THAT page down to fit the sheet so nothing is clipped or overlapped — but it then renders visibly smaller/denser than the others, so pace your content across pages rather than relying on it. • FILL each page — a `.ds-page` occupies a WHOLE A4 sheet whether or not its content fills it, so a page left half-empty prints as a big blank band at the bottom and reads as a mistake, not restraint. Pace and size content (type scale, spacing, columns, where you break) so every page is ROUGHLY FULL; only the FINAL page should be partial. Never orphan a lone heading or a few trailing lines onto an otherwise-empty sheet — if a page is coming up short, tighten the split, pull content forward, or loosen spacing to fill it. Balanced, full pages are what separates a designed document from an exported one. • Do NOT hard-pin `.ds-page` to `height:1123px` — set its A4 size via `min-height` (or just let DocStash supply it) so a slightly-too-tall page can breathe instead of trapping/overlapping content. Absolutely-positioned footers/page numbers should sit at the page BOTTOM via the flow, not a fixed `height`. • Do NOT style the `` background, the margins AROUND the paper, or scrolling — DocStash owns the canvas + chrome and overrides them. Style only the INTERIOR of each `.ds-page` (its own padding, type, color, layout); you MAY bleed to the page edge inside a `.ds-page`. • Self-contained: inline all `

tools.name: create_docx
tools.description:
Generate an EDITABLE Word document (.docx) for DocStash and show the user an INLINE PREVIEW — a reflowable Word doc on a US-Letter page (1" margins). Use this when the user specifically wants a WORD doc / editable .docx; for a DESIGNED, print-perfect document use `create_pdf` instead. `content` = MARKDOWN — the renderer walks it straight to a real .docx. The browser renders it at view time — do NOT generate a binary.
  Author rich markdown (don't flatten to plain text). Mapped to native Word: headings (#..###### → real Heading styles a TOC can use), **bold**/*italic*/~~strike~~, `inline code` + ```fenced blocks```, ordered/unordered (nested) lists, tables, blockquotes, links, images (![alt](https-url), embedded at view time), ==highlight==, <u>underline</u>, footnotes (text[^1] + [^1]: note), and a page break via a lone ---pagebreak--- (or \f, or <!-- pagebreak -->). IMAGE URLS MUST BE DIRECT FILES — the response must BE the image bytes; any page/gallery/viewer link (commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:… , unsplash.com/photos/…) serves HTML and renders BROKEN. With web search available, SEARCH FIRST and take the exact filename/id from a result ("site:commons.wikimedia.org <subject>") — recalled filenames are frequently misspelled or nonexistent. KNOWN-GOOD DIRECT FORMATS: Wikimedia → commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:FilePath/<File_Name.ext>?width=1600 (build from just the filename; never hand-construct upload.wikimedia.org hashed/thumb paths) · Unsplash → images.unsplash.com/photo-<id>?w=1600&q=80&auto=format · Pexels → images.pexels.com/photos/<id>/<name>.jpeg?auto=compress&w=1600 · placeholder photo → picsum.photos/seed/<any-word>/1600/900 (seeded = stable) · flat placeholder → placehold.co/1600x900.png (keep the .png — the bare URL serves SVG, which Word embedding rejects). Unsure a real image exists → prefer the placeholders over guessing. SIZE: request ~1200-1600px via those params — full-resolution scans bloat the doc for no visible gain.

Show the user an INLINE PREVIEW of what you author here — nothing is stashed yet. Author the content YOURSELF as `content` — never via a binary generator (DocStash renders the real file at view time). Then STOP — do NOT call `stash` yourself: the user reviews the preview and stashes it, or explicitly tells you to (save / publish / ship it). NO SELF-ATTRIBUTION: the output is the user's own work — never add a "Made with…" / "Generated by AI" footer, byline, badge, or watermark unless they explicitly ask. SLUG IS CRITICAL — it cuts BOTH ways. Pass the SAME slug to iterate the SAME versioned URL; OMIT it to create a NEW document. Passing the wrong slug OVERWRITES the wrong doc; omitting it while iterating spawns a DUPLICATE. PASS the slug when: you JUST showed a preview via a create_* tool and the user asks for another version / a change / an update / a fix / a tweak of THAT SAME thing (pass the slug THAT call just returned), OR a doc already exists that they want to revise — one you fetched with a `get_*` show tool or `read_document`, a doc they named, or whose docstash URL they shared. OMIT the slug when the user wants ANOTHER document, a SECOND thing, or a DIFFERENT TYPE — a new doc / page / app / sheet is ALWAYS a fresh doc even in the same chat, so do NOT carry over the slug the previous preview returned. A DIFFERENT tool/type is a dead giveaway it's a NEW doc: reusing another type's slug would overwrite it. Rule of thumb: treat "another / a new / a different / also make / now make" as NEW (omit slug); treat "change it / update it / fix it / this one / that version" as SAME (pass slug). When genuinely unsure, prefer creating a new doc over silently overwriting an existing one. (Full lifecycle / organization / public-link rules are in the DocStash server instructions.)

tools.name: create_sheet
tools.description:
Generate a SPREADSHEET / WORKBOOK (Excel) for DocStash and show the user an INLINE PREVIEW. `content` = JSON.stringify(SheetSpec) — do NOT generate an .xlsx binary; the browser renders real Excel at view time. Spec schema below.

Show the user an INLINE PREVIEW of what you author here — nothing is stashed yet. Author the content YOURSELF as `content` — never via a binary generator (DocStash renders the real file at view time). Then STOP — do NOT call `stash` yourself: the user reviews the preview and stashes it, or explicitly tells you to (save / publish / ship it). NO SELF-ATTRIBUTION: the output is the user's own work — never add a "Made with…" / "Generated by AI" footer, byline, badge, or watermark unless they explicitly ask. SLUG IS CRITICAL — it cuts BOTH ways. Pass the SAME slug to iterate the SAME versioned URL; OMIT it to create a NEW document. Passing the wrong slug OVERWRITES the wrong doc; omitting it while iterating spawns a DUPLICATE. PASS the slug when: you JUST showed a preview via a create_* tool and the user asks for another version / a change / an update / a fix / a tweak of THAT SAME thing (pass the slug THAT call just returned), OR a doc already exists that they want to revise — one you fetched with a `get_*` show tool or `read_document`, a doc they named, or whose docstash URL they shared. OMIT the slug when the user wants ANOTHER document, a SECOND thing, or a DIFFERENT TYPE — a new doc / page / app / sheet is ALWAYS a fresh doc even in the same chat, so do NOT carry over the slug the previous preview returned. A DIFFERENT tool/type is a dead giveaway it's a NEW doc: reusing another type's slug would overwrite it. Rule of thumb: treat "another / a new / a different / also make / now make" as NEW (omit slug); treat "change it / update it / fix it / this one / that version" as SAME (pass slug). When genuinely unsure, prefer creating a new doc over silently overwriting an existing one. (Full lifecycle / organization / public-link rules are in the DocStash server instructions.)

XLSX SPEC SHAPE (when kind='xlsx'):
  { theme?: '<preset>' | { custom theme }, sheets: [ Sheet, ... ] }   — 1-20 sheets per workbook. A custom theme is a FLAT object (fields at top level, NOT nested under `custom`): { headerBackground, headerText, text, stripe, border, accent, font? }.
  Sheet: { name, rows: Row[], columnWidths?: number[], rowHeights?: number[], frozenRows?: number, frozenCols?: number, merges?: string[], autoFilter?: string, conditionalFormats?: CF[], charts?: Chart[] }
    • name         — tab label, ≤31 chars; avoid [ ] : * ? / and \
    • rows         — top-to-bottom; each row is an array of cells (rows may be ragged — short rows pad empty on the right)
    • columnWidths — left→right, Excel char-width units; omit to auto-fit
    • rowHeights   — top→bottom, in points; omit/null an entry to keep default height
    • frozenRows / frozenCols — sticky header rows / label columns that stay visible while scrolling
    • merges       — A1 ranges to merge, e.g. ['A1:D1','A2:A5']; top-left cell's value/format wins (great for spanning titles)
    • autoFilter   — A1 range to attach Excel filter dropdowns, e.g. 'A1:F1' (header) or 'A1:F100' (whole block)
    • conditionalFormats — declarative rules (heatmaps, bars, icons, threshold highlights); see CF below
  Cell — a BARE value for the common case, or an OBJECT when you need a formula / formatting / comment:
    bare:   string | number | boolean | null
    object: { value?, formula?, result?, format?, comment?, hyperlink?, validation? }
      • formula   — Excel formula starting '=', e.g. '=SUM(B2:B10)', '=IF(A1>0,"yes","no")', cross-sheet '=Sheet2!B5*1.1' (overrides value)
      • result    — IMPORTANT cached formula value: ALWAYS supply the computed result alongside `formula`, else many viewers show the cell BLANK until they recalc. (You may instead pass `value` next to `formula` as the cache.)
      • hyperlink — makes the cell a clickable link; its `value` is the display text
      • validation — { type:'list'|'decimal'|'whole'|'date', values?, min?, max?, allowBlank?, prompt?, error? }; 'list'+values gives a dropdown
  format (CellFormat): { bold?, italic?, underline?, strikethrough?, color?, background?, fontFamily?, align?: 'left'|'center'|'right', valign?: 'top'|'middle'|'bottom', numberFormat?, fontSize?, wrapText?, border? }
    • color / background — hex '#RRGGBB' OR a theme token (color: 'text'|'accent';  background: 'headerBackground'|'stripe'|'accent')
    • fontFamily   — per-cell font override (e.g. 'Arial','Courier New'); defaults to the theme font
    • numberFormat — Excel format string: '#,##0' int · '#,##0.00' 2dp · '$#,##0' currency · '0.00%' percent · 'yyyy-mm-dd' date · '@' force-text
    • border — per side { top?, right?, bottom?, left? }; each side is `true` (thin, theme color) OR { style?:'thin'|'medium'|'thick'|'double'|'dashed', color? }
  CF (Sheet.conditionalFormats[]): { range:'B2:B100', type:'colorScale'|'dataBar'|'iconSet'|'cellIs'|'expression', ...rule }
    • colorScale — colors?: 2-3 hex low→high (default red→yellow→green heatmap)
    • dataBar    — color?: hex bar color (default theme accent)
    • iconSet    — iconSet?: '3TrafficLights1'|'3Arrows'|'5Rating'|... (default '3TrafficLights1')
    • cellIs     — operator:'greaterThan'|'lessThan'|'greaterThanOrEqual'|'lessThanOrEqual'|'equal'|'notEqual'|'between', value, value2?(for between), background?/fontColor?
    • expression — formula:'$B2>$C2' (no leading '='), background?/fontColor? applied where TRUE
  Chart (Sheet.charts[]): { type: 'bar'|'line'|'pie'|'area'|'scatter', title?, dataRange: 'A1:B10', categoriesRange?, position: { fromRow, fromCol, cols, rows } }  — rendered as a native Excel chart in the download.
  CONVENTION — the FIRST row of each sheet is treated as the themed header. Put values/formulas as raw numbers (not pre-formatted strings) and let `numberFormat` style them, so totals/charts compute. For any `formula`, also pass its computed `result` so the workbook isn't blank on first open.
  Theme presets:
    • 'minimal' — Clean header bar (navy blue + white text), light gray stripes, sans-serif. Safe default for most data.
    • 'corporate' — Deep blue header, white text, subtle stripes, Calibri. Standard business workbook look.
    • 'finance' — Dark green header (currency-feel), white text, no stripes, Calibri. Financial models / accounting.
    • 'research' — Charcoal header, off-white text, off-white stripes, Helvetica narrow. Academic / data-research vibe.
    • 'minimal_dark' — Dark slate background throughout, light text, subtle border. Dark-mode tables.
  Minimal example (JSON.stringify this): {"theme":"finance","sheets":[{"name":"Q3","frozenRows":1,"rows":[["Item","Revenue"],["Subscriptions",{"value":42000,"format":{"numberFormat":"$#,##0"}}],["Total",{"formula":"=SUM(B2:B2)","format":{"bold":true,"numberFormat":"$#,##0"}}]]}]}

tools.name: create_app
tools.description:
Generate a LIVE WEB APP (a multi-file bundle) for DocStash and show the user an INLINE PREVIEW. Use this ONLY when you're genuinely shipping MULTIPLE files (e.g. index.html + a separate app.js + styles.css + local assets). For a single self-contained page, use `create_page` instead — it has no bundle, so it can't fail on a missing local file.
Deliver the finished app THROUGH this tool — DocStash hosts the bundle live at a shareable URL. Do NOT leave it as a local file/artifact or paste the files into the chat.

Pass `files: { "path/to/file": "<contents>", ... }`; the MCP server zips in-memory and uploads as a bundle. YOU MUST declare:
  - `entry`    — the file the runtime mounts (e.g. 'index.html' for a static site, 'app.py' for a python script).
  - `language` — the RUNTIME token: 'static' (HTML+CSS+JS), 'python', 'ruby', 'php', 'lua', 'go', 'rust', 'cpp', 'java', etc.
  - `framework` — declare this WHENEVER the bundle uses any of these (lower-case, exact token): 'react' / 'vue' / 'svelte' / 'solid' / 'preact' / 'angular' / 'lit' / 'htmx' / 'alpine' / 'qwik' / 'astro' / 'three' (THREE.js / 3D animations / WebGL scenes) / 'p5' (p5.js / generative art / creative-coding) / 'd3' (D3.js / data viz / charts) / 'jquery'. Pick ONE — the primary library the app is built around. Drives the dashboard card chip.
    Examples:
      - HTML page imports Three.js to render a rotating cube → framework: 'three'
      - React app with a useState counter                   → framework: 'react'
      - p5.js sketch of bouncing particles                  → framework: 'p5'
      - Plain HTML + CSS + a tiny <script> tag, no library  → omit `framework` entirely
    Omit ONLY when the bundle uses NO known framework. Don't guess — you just generated the files, you know which library is in there. Realistic for agent-generated apps: typically 10-50 KB of text, fits in one tool call.
BUILD-FREE RULE (language='static') — the bundle is served to the browser EXACTLY as uploaded; there is NO build step. Do NOT ship a framework SOURCE project: no `.svelte` / `.vue` / `.ts` / `.tsx` files, no Vite/webpack config expecting compilation (the browser can't load those as `<script type="module">`, and DocStash won't compile them — the app fails with a 'module script … MIME text/html' error). For Svelte / React / Vue / Solid, either (a) inline a PREBUILT single bundle of plain .js/.css into `index.html`, or (b) import the framework from a CDN as ESM, e.g. `import { mount } from 'https://esm.sh/svelte'`. STRONGLY PREFER esm.sh — it serves correct, CORS-safe, versioned ESM, React included: `import React from 'https://esm.sh/react@18'` + `import { createRoot } from 'https://esm.sh/react-dom@18/client'`, mounted from a `<script type=module>`. AVOID the in-browser Babel transformer (@babel/standalone + a `text/babel` script): it's slow and the #1 runtime failure. And DON'T load React/ReactDOM from cdnjs UMD unless the path includes `/umd/` (…/react/18.2.0/umd/react.production.min.js) — omitting `umd/` 404s, the 404 HTML comes back as a non-executable script, and the app dies with 'React is not defined'.
MODULE-FORMAT CHECKLIST (these three console errors mean you authored a BUILD-STEP/bundler app the runtime can't run) — (1) `Unexpected token 'export'` / (2) `Cannot use import statement outside a module`: a file using `import`/`export` (e.g. an esm.sh module or your own code) was loaded as a CLASSIC script. EVERY file that uses `import`/`export` MUST be loaded via `<script type="module">`; a bare `<script src=…>` at an ESM module throws these. (3) `Unexpected token '<'`: a referenced local JS path (a build output like `/src/main.jsx`, `/assets/index-*.js`, or an extensionless `/client` entry) isn't in the bundle, so the static runtime SPA-falls-back and serves your index.html for that request — the browser then parses HTML as JS. NEVER reference build-output paths; only reference files you actually put in `files`, or absolute CDN URLs. If you'd hit any of these, re-author as EITHER a single self-contained page (prefer `create_page`) OR a bundle whose every script is inline or a `type=module` CDN-ESM import.
SELF-CONTAINED BUNDLE RULE — the bundle must stand alone. Every LOCAL URL your entry references (scripts, styles, images, fonts) MUST be a key in `files`. For every asset you have exactly three valid choices: (a) inline it, (b) include it in `files`, or (c) load it from an absolute CDN URL (https://…). NEVER reference a local path you didn't write. In particular, do NOT add `<link rel="icon" href="/favicon.ico">` (or any icon/manifest link) unless you actually include that file — a stray local ref is the #1 cause of broken bundles. IMAGE URLS MUST BE DIRECT FILES — the response must BE the image bytes; any page/gallery/viewer link (commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:… , unsplash.com/photos/…) serves HTML and renders BROKEN. With web search available, SEARCH FIRST and take the exact filename/id from a result ("site:commons.wikimedia.org <subject>") — recalled filenames are frequently misspelled or nonexistent. KNOWN-GOOD DIRECT FORMATS: Wikimedia → commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:FilePath/<File_Name.ext>?width=1600 (build from just the filename; never hand-construct upload.wikimedia.org hashed/thumb paths) · Unsplash → images.unsplash.com/photo-<id>?w=1600&q=80&auto=format · Pexels → images.pexels.com/photos/<id>/<name>.jpeg?auto=compress&w=1600 · placeholder photo → picsum.photos/seed/<any-word>/1600/900 (seeded = stable) · flat placeholder → placehold.co/1600x900.png (keep the .png — the bare URL serves SVG, which Word embedding rejects). Unsure a real image exists → prefer the placeholders over guessing. SIZE: request ~1200-1600px via those params — full-resolution scans bloat the doc for no visible gain.

RESPONSIVE RULE — for HTML pages and any HTML inside an app bundle: the page MUST be responsive and scroll on mobile. Include `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`, use natural document flow, and DON'T lock the page to `height:100vh` + `overflow:hidden` (that traps scrolling on phones). The viewer renders your page full-width with no extra scroll container.

tools.name: stash
tools.description: STASH a preview (from a create_* tool) to DocStash — this is the actual SAVE, and the saved doc stays PRIVATE. The `slug` IS the doc's slug: it creates the doc on that slug, or pushes a NEW VERSION if the preview targeted an existing doc. ‼️ Do NOT call this automatically right after a create_* call — a plain 'create / generate X' request is fully satisfied by the preview alone. Call it ONLY when the user EXPLICITLY signals saving (save / stash / ship it / keep it / looks good) or clicks Stash in the inline preview. When in doubt, ask first. Returns the doc's `url`. ‼️ Stashing does NOT PUBLISH: the url opens only for you + anyone you've granted access. If the user asked to PUBLISH / make public / get a public shareable link, stash first (this), then call `manage_sharing` action='set-public'.

name.description: Optional override for the doc name at save time (new docs only).

description.description: Optional one-line changelog OVERRIDE. Prefer setting this on the create_* tool instead — a changelog set here is lost if the user stashes the preview manually. Only use this to override the preview's stored changelog at save time.
